head: edb086aa3c103e2bb0815270b008a85e090d59a2
classification_reasons: Blast radius: lesson_and_eval runs at gate (e) for every entry_route == incident change on every project pinned to this plugin version; a mistake in checks.py or index.py parks or silently stops protecting the lesson/eval invariant across all future incidents, not just this PR.
New generated artifact and markdown/YAML convention (lessons/index.md, lesson frontmatter) with cross-platform (Windows/Linux) determinism requirements — not a small, self-contained edit.

Spec is tight for this round specifically (five named findings, each with a named fix and a named test, no open concern), but the plan as a whole still carries prior Flagged concerns history and a non-routine iteration cap (2) already in force in status.yaml, which this round operates under.
attempted: Intent: confirmed this round's five edits (import de-duplication in checks.py, markdown link/target escaping in index.py, moving lessons_dir.mkdir out of build()/check(), a run-1 sources example in template/lessons/README.md, and the 'missing or not a <kind>' wording in checks.py) are exactly what the owner's PR #132 review (#5455893201) asked for -- read fix-requests.json and fix-response.md and matched each item against the actual diff hunks in plugin/gate/checks.py, plugin/lessons/index.py and template/lessons/README.md. No scope drift: nothing beyond the five items was touched (the six 'can wait for 0.3.7' items from the owner's prior review were correctly left out, and two draft edits to docs/OPERATING_MODEL.md/comments were reverted, confirmed by that file's diff hunk still reading the unfixed 'a heading per tag' wording).

Spec and plan: spec.md and plan.md are unchanged in this round's diff, matching the owner's explicit instruction ('No change to spec.md (choice 164)') and fix-response.md's claim that plan.md's file list already covers this round's files as a subset. Verified plan.md/spec.md diff hunks visible in diff-e.patch belong to an earlier round (the 9th supersedes fail case sync), not this one.

Proof: read the literal plugin/gate/checks.py and plugin/lessons/index.py diff hunks directly -- the single module-level `from lessons import index as lessons_mod` import replaces both former local imports; `_escape_link_text`/`_escape_link_target` are applied in `_render_line` and `_render_unsorted_line`; `lessons_dir.mkdir(...)` is removed from `build()` and added only in `main`'s build branch; `_lesson_field_problems` now reports 'missing or not a <kind>'. Matched each to a new, exact-assertion unit test (test_a_title_with_markdown_link_characters_renders_as_one_link, test_check_on_a_root_without_lessons_leaves_no_lessons_behind, test_lesson_and_eval_fails_on_a_wrong_type_frontmatter_field, test_lessons_readme_sources_example_includes_a_run_n_entry). evidence/test.log's first line is literal toolchain output (not a 'deferred' placeholder) timestamped to match status.yaml's gate time, 1436 passed exit 0; build.log and lint.log likewise exit 0 clean. evidence/verifier.md is from an earlier fix round (HEAD 00ddfc7) and does not itself exercise this round's five edits, but each edit has its own exact-output unit test that ran in the same green 1436-test suite, which is stronger proof for this kind of mechanical change than a fresh verifier narrative would add; noted but not treated as a gap.

Blast radius: confirmed the diff touches no guardrail file (CLAUDE.md, .claude/**, REVIEW.md, root sdlc.yaml) and no sdlc.yaml: risk_list item; template/sdlc.yaml and docs/OPERATING_MODEL.md are plugin-shipped content per the plan, not this repo's own guardrails, and neither was edited by this round anyway. Checked that removing the two local imports does not introduce a circular import (plugin/lessons/index.py only imports state.yamlish) and that check()'s no-mkdir behavior doesn't regress the CLI build path (main's build branch still creates lessons/ before writing).

Policies: no stored personal/sensitive field added; no auth/money/production-config/migration path touched (data-conventions, risk_list both clear). definition-of-done's split between deterministic gate checks and advisory judgment is respected -- this round only tightens wording and fixes two real bugs (link-breaking characters, a side-effecting read-only check), it does not add new policy-relevant surface.

Tests: checked that the wrong-type-field test and the escaping test assert exact strings/lines (not just 'no crash'), so they could not pass with the bug still present; checked that no pre-existing test assertion was weakened -- the one existing wording assertion in test_gate.py was updated to the new, equally-specific wording, and the existing missing-lesson glob/fail-case tests are untouched.
